newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo firms agree $75 mln barter deals with China.
newsitem.headline: Yugo firms agree $75 mln barter deals with China.

text.p: Serbia's oil company NIS Jugopetrol has signed $75 million worth of deals with several firms for exports of Yugoslav goods to China within a barter arrangement, Belgrade newspapers reported on Thursday.

The deals are part of a $330 million barter arrangement signed in March between Jugopetrol, a subsidiary of Naftna Industrija Srbije (NIS), and the Chinese petroleum corporation Sinochem under which two million tonnes of crude oil will be imported from China in exchange for Yugoslav products.
Nobody at NIS Jugopetrol was available for comment.
The $75 million deals were agreed with the Serbian firms Sartid 1913, Zmaj, Viskoza and Ivo Lola Ribar.

Contracts would also be signed soon with a group of producers headed by Industrija Motora i Traktora (IMT) worth around $40 million, and with Sever Subotica for around $10 million, the Belgrade daily Politika reported.
A Chinese delegation was due next week to sign an agreement with 14. Oktobar from Krusevac for another $25 million worth of exports, it said.

"By the end of the year, we will have export deals worth around $150 million, and since Jugopetrol has drawn $107 million worth of oil from China so far, we are approaching a balance," Dragan Tomic, NIS Jugopetrol director and Serbian parliament speaker, was quoted as saying.

Politika said Beobanka would soon sign a separate agreement for use of funds which, under a Serbian government decision, will be set aside for production earmarked for export within the barter arrangement.
"Real funds have been secured for the volume of deals achieved so far," the bank's general director Zlatan Perucic was quoted as saying. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
